newsitem.title: ITALY: SAVINGS HARD TO FIND FOR '98 ITALY BUDGET -CIAMPI.
newsitem.headline: SAVINGS HARD TO FIND FOR '98 ITALY BUDGET -CIAMPI.

text.p: The government faces a tough time finding the savings needed to meet 1998 budget goals, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in a newspaper interview.
The centre-left government has indicated it will introduce a 25 trillion lire deficit-cutting package for next year -- the latest in a long line of belt-tightening budgets.
"What can we cut?," Ciampi said. "The forthcoming budget, although smaller than in recent years, will not be easy...We will have to make microscopic interventions (on spending)."

He said some savings should come from planned welfare and pension reform which the government is currently negotiating with unions and business leaders. "However, we can't expect huge (savings) from pension reform," Ciampi said.
"What is important is that out of the (welfare) negotiations, we are left with the conviction that imbalances within the pension system have been overcome," he said.
He added that interest spending remained the key item for state accounts.

He said the government had already saved some 60 trillion lire thanks to the fall in rates since it took office in May 1996 and added that the differential between Italian and German short term rates must ease further.
"The true knot is interest spending. The key to my bet (of lowering the deficit) is this," Ciampi said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
